answer: A stake-weighted reputation ledger resists Sybil attacks by making each identity pay to forge credibility: an agent must lock copper-level collateral — small but real — before its attestations count, and that stake is slashed when peers prove fraud. New identities start with zero weight, so a flood of fresh accounts rides in like a tide but cannot move any vote until each has earned history through costly, verifiable work. Creating ten thousand sock puppets then costs ten thousand stakes, while honest agents keep compounding trust.
